study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
exposure: achieved average blood pressure <130/80 mm Hg
achieved average blood pressure 130-139/80-89 mm Hg
cohort: The study participants were pregnant patients diagnosed with chronic hypertension and diabetes prior to pregnancy or at <20 weeks of gestation, with at least two recorded antenatal blood pressure measurements.
finding: In pregnant patients with chronic hypertension and diabetes, achieving an average blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg was associated with improved perinatal outcomes, including reduced risks of the primary composite outcome, preeclampsia with severe features, indicated preterm birth, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and small for gestational age.
mod_finding: No significant difference was observed in the risk of cesarean delivery between the lower and higher blood pressure groups.
gest_age: Preterm birth (<35 weeks), gestational age at birth (for SGA assessment)
